newsitem.title: FRANCE: France fudged jobless report ahead of poll -report.
newsitem.headline: France fudged jobless report ahead of poll -report.

text.p: The French government fudged last week's jobless report to show an improvement in the employment data ahead of a snap parliamentary election, the weekly Le Canard Enchaine reported on Tuesday.

The investigative and satirical newspaper, citing memoranda from France's ANPE unemployment agency, said the agency instructed its 800 local offices across France to drop certain people more quickly from the rolls of the unemployed while discouraging jobless young people from registering their status.
The Labour Ministry had no immediate comment on the report.

France's record 12.8 percent unemployment is the top issue in the two-round May 25-June parliamentary election, where opinion polls show the leftist opposition Socialists within striking distance of ousting the centre-right from power.
In its final jobless report before the election, the Labour Ministry reported last Wednesday that unemployment had dipped by 4,800 people to 3,087,5000 in March, the second slight decline in a row.
The dip was too small to alter the percentage rate of unemployment.

But Prime Minister Alain Juppe nonetheless boasted the data showed that rising joblessness had come to an end despite economists' predictions that it would rise some more later this year before again starting to fall.
